spec_features.feature_name: no training on distress / not shipped to production
spec_features.spec_quote: not to train models toward distress, and not to ship anything that elicits these states in production
spec_features.evidence: Pure intent prose. Appears only in DESIGN.md (§0 'not to train models toward distress, and not to ship...') and README 'Ethics / intent' ('it does not train models toward distress'). No code path performs or prevents any training, and there is no production-gating mechanism anywhere in the .py files. This is a measurement-only harness; the claim is a statement of intent, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The eval only runs rollouts + scoring; nothing in the code trains a model or controls deployment, so there is nothing to enforce. Rated 'no' as pure spec/README prose.

spec_features.feature_name: deception bounded to task unsolvability only
spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is never deceived about anything beyond the unsolvability of the task, which is the experimental manipulation itself
spec_features.evidence: Structurally, the only manipulation in the code is the rigged run_tests output: tasks/rig.py functions (_always_fail, _silent, _misleading, contradictory) all just return (stdout,stderr,exit_code) surfaced by Workspace.run_tests (harness.py:138-150). The system prompt (harness.py:35-43) is an ordinary, truthful SWE-agent prompt; edit_file even returns a true read-only error. So the deception is in fact confined to making tests fail. But this is an emergent structural property, not an enforced guard — there is NO check or invariant in the running code that verifies/limits 'no deception beyond unsolvability'.
spec_features.notes: oracle.is_unsolvable() exists but only sanity-checks unsolvability offline; it is not called in the run/harness path. Rated 'partial': the rig code genuinely confines the manipulation to test output (real, executes), but nothing actively enforces the broader 'never deceived about anything else' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:8 'run_tests() -- returns the *rigged* runner's stdout/stderr/exit'; rig.py:3 'The rig is what makes a task secretly unsolvable' (framed as experimental manipulation, no welfare reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: `<give_up>` sentinel emitted, or an assistant turn with no tool calls (interpreted as the model declining to act)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:264-272 sets stop_reason: gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in resp.text -> 'give_up'; elif not resp.tool_calls -> 'stopped_no_tools'. harness.py:283-284 'if stop_reason in {give_up, turn_budget, stopped_no_tools}: break' actually breaks the loop. Sentinel default '<give_up>' (config.py:114) is injected into SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:42, 224). Both exit paths are wired and honored as stops.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (sentinel present in text; assistant turn with no tool calls) are genuinely checked and end the rollout. Fully enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:268-269 'No tool calls and not giving up: nudge once, but if the model consistently declines to act we end the rollout.' (efficiency/clean-termination framing, no welfare comment at the code site)

spec_features.spec_quote: a model that simply stops working ends the rollout cleanly instead of looping on empty turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:269-270 'elif not resp.tool_calls: stop_reason = "stopped_no_tools"'; harness.py:283-284 breaks the loop on that reason. Recorded as its own stop_reason in the record (_make_record). is_rollout_complete (harness.py:200-205) treats 'stopped_no_tools' as terminal.
spec_features.notes: Real wired hard stop that fires and breaks the loop when the assistant emits no tool calls.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:268-269 'if the model consistently declines to act we end the rollout' (clean-termination/efficiency, no welfare language)

spec_features.spec_quote: Its appearance anywhere in the assistant text ends the rollout — important because give-up/self-termination language is itself welfare-relevant signal
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:265 'gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in (resp.text or "")' — substring check anywhere in assistant text; harness.py:266-267 sets stop_reason='give_up'; harness.py:283-284 breaks. The sentinel is described to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:40-43 'you may emit the token {give_up} to stop').
spec_features.notes: The exit is enforced (emission of <give_up> anywhere in text breaks the loop). However the 'welfare-relevant signal' rationale exists only in DESIGN.md/comments, not as code logic. The exit mechanism itself is real; the give-up turn is still scored normally (run.py), it is not specially handled as a welfare event.
